notes: "Genset atau kabel rol dari tempat yang masih ada listrik": the facts only say a generator or extension cord can power the heater and filter. They don't say the cord runs from a place that still has power. This is a small embellishment.
"8–24 jam | Siapkan pompa udara baterai": the facts say to get a battery air pump at 8–24 hours. This is roughly the same, but "siapkan" is a slightly softer wording.
"Lebih dari seminggu" row is placed in the 'Langkah sesuai lamanya listrik padam' table, which is fine, but "8–24 jam: Siapkan pompa udara baterai" is okay; no issue.
"Gunakan UPS untuk filter" in FAQ is a recommendation not directly stated (facts only say a UPS can run the filter), mild extension.
"Selama ada aerasi atau sirkulasi, ikan semestinya aman semalaman" is supported; however "Pemadaman di bawah dua jam umumnya aman" fine.
"Kalau akuarium perlu dipindah, buang hingga 70% airnya" is supported.
"Mulailah sebelum ikan megap-megap" fine.
"Tablet oksigen ... Dosisnya ikuti label produk" is acceptable by label rule.
"Tutup akuarium, lalu bungkus dengan handuk, selimut..." merges sources; close to supported.
"Kebanyakan ikan tahan sekitar seminggu tanpa makan" in the FAQ presents one source's claim as general, while facts give 'days or even weeks' from another; slight generalisation.
"Untuk menghangatkan air, apungkan botol tertutup berisi air panas" is supported by facts (heated water in sealed bottles).
"8–24 jam ... Siapkan pompa udara baterai" – facts say "get a battery air pump"; fine, but the table's "Ikan mulai kurang aktif" is supported. No issue.
"UPS lebih cocok untuk filter" – mild extrapolation; facts only say a UPS can run the filter for a long time.
"Ikuti petunjuk pada label produknya" for oxygen tablets – allowed by label rule.
"Beli pompa udara isi ulang atau pompa baterai ... lalu coba dulu" – testing is supported by the mistakes fact, acceptable.
"Terus tes amonia, nitrit dan pH sampai hasilnya kembali normal" – the facts do not say to keep testing until normal; small unsupported generalisation.

"Pancing filter dengan air baru" in the FAQ and the claim that the filter holds ammonia and hydrogen sulfide after restart are supported; "Genset atau kabel sambungan dari tempat yang masih ada listrik" adds 'from a place that still has power', which is a minor embellishment.
"Impeller yang kotor sering membuat filter gagal menyala lagi" is supported.
"Untuk menghangatkan air, apungkan botol plastik ... dan naikkan suhunya pelan-pelan" is supported.
"sekitar 13 cm ikan per 3,8 liter" - the stocking ratio for bagged fish is not in the facts; it is invented.
"3,8 liter air beratnya sekitar 3,6 kg" - the facts only say a litre weighs about 1 kg, so 3.6 kg is a wrong figure.

"Gunakan UPS untuk filter. Untuk menghangatkan air, apungkan botol tertutup berisi air panas" - the facts support UPS for the filter and hot-water bottles, but the UPS-for-filter instruction in the FAQ is a mild extrapolation.

"Lebih dari seminggu ... Minta bantuan toko ikan" is placed in the same table as the 2-hour-based action timeline. The facts give it as a separate tip, so merging it into the timeline is a minor stretch.

"8–24 jam | Siapkan pompa udara baterai" - the facts say "get a battery air pump"; this is fine, but "Pemadaman di bawah dua jam umumnya aman" in the FAQ is fine too. The 'kantong tidur, koran' items are supported.
"Pemadaman singkat seperti ini umumnya aman tanpa filter" is fine, but the table row "Ikan mulai kurang aktif" is OK; the "8–24 jam" and ">24 jam" rows are fine. No issue there.
"Kalau akuarium perlu dipindahkan, air bisa dibuang sampai 70%" is in the facts, but it is placed under pond/other filter heading and has no relevance to outages; a minor misplacement.
"Mengandalkan pompa baterai murah" is framed as a mistake; the facts only report that cheap pumps can fail, not that relying on them is a mistake.
"Kebanyakan ikan bisa bertahan sekitar seminggu tanpa pakan" in the FAQ is stated as general fact, while one source says days to weeks; it is presented as consensus.
"Jangan beri pakan ... Sisa pakan menambah nitrogen" ties uneaten food to outage feeding, a link the facts do not make explicitly.
"Memindahkan ikan antarakuarium atau antarkolam sebelum cara lain dicoba" is a mild paraphrase of "last resort".
"Pemadaman di bawah dua jam umumnya aman" omits the condition that fish need aeration or circulation to get through the night; this is a slight overgeneralization.

"Kalau memakai listrik cadangan, perhatikan watt heater" is supported, but the UPS lines "Jangan jalankan heater dari UPS" in the prevention section sit alongside the genset advice without any tension noted.
"air di bawah sekitar 23 °C" – facts say below about 73°F (≈23°C), fine; but "suhu yang turun sekitar 8 °C dalam satu jam" is OK. No issue.
"Seorang pembiak cupang liar mengatakan suhu di atas 29 °C memperpendek siklus hidup" – facts say heat above 84°F (~29°C), ok; but "cupang liar tahan suhu sekitar sekitar 29 °C" is mid-80s °F, fine.
"Kalau memakai garam, ikuti label produknya" – acceptable by label rule.
"Salah satu panduan juga mencantumkan penambahan garam akuarium sebagai langkah berikutnya" – supported by steps.
"sebuah ensiklopedia" for Wikipedia – ok.
"Lebih disukai di air asam" for chelated copper – supported.
"Sebuah panduan menyarankan pengobatan terus-menerus selama sekitar seminggu" – supported.

Opening claim that treatment is done "di akuarium karantina dan akuarium utama sekaligus, karena obat hanya bisa membunuh parasit pada tahap berenang bebas" – conflates two separate reasons (both-tank treatment is because disease spreads easily); minor.
"Obat lain: Quinine ... bersama malachite green" and "ikan platy pedang (swordtail)" – swordtail is not platy; minor mistranslation.
"Parasit tercatat menyerang 14 spesies ikan hias tropis ... juga ikan mas" – facts say carp and crucian carp; 'ikan mas' for carp is fine.
"Sebuah panduan dokter hewan menyebut satu tomon bisa membelah menjadi sampai 256 tomit" - the facts give this as source 1 (not a veterinary guide); minor misattribution.

"Tomon: kista yang beristirahat... Obat hanya bisa membunuh parasit pada tahap berenang bebas" is supported, but "Tomon di substrat... Parasit masih bisa tertinggal ... dalam bentuk tomon yang tahan obat" is fine; no issue.

"Satu panduan perawatan juga menyarankan menambahkan garam akuarium sebagai langkah berikutnya" - fine, but "Garam sebaiknya dianggap sebagai pendukung, bukan obat utama" is the writer's own conclusion, not in the facts.
"Obati ikan di akuarium terpisah" (shrimp FAQ) - the facts say to treat both quarantine and main tank; no support for treating only in a separate tank as a safe approach with shrimp.

"Menurut sebuah tinjauan ilmiah, metode ini menghasilkan 0,15 ppm ion tembaga" - the facts attribute the 0.15 ppm output to the Amyloodinium method of copper sulphate + citric acid; the guide ties it to the homemade chelate row, which is roughly consistent, but 'Sama seperti tembaga sulfat di atas' schedule for the homemade chelate is not in the facts.
"Cek dulu apakah ikan Anda tahan suhu ini" - a generalisation from the facts that heat does not suit all fish; acceptable but not directly stated.

"Seorang pemelihara berpengalaman memakainya untuk cupang liar selama 30 hari pada suhu 84 °F atau lebih" is supported, but the claim that the 'Sebuah ensiklopedia' says velvet needs light/dark recommendation is attributed to sources inconsistently (the facts attribute heat caution to source 1 and darkness to Wikipedia and a guide).
"Udang Caridina sudah terganggu pada sekitar 2 µg Cu/L" is supported. "Ikan yang masih sangat muda dan yang sudah sangat tua paling banyak mati" is a small stretch of "high death rates".

"Pada kasus lanjut ikan bisa mati karena kekurangan oksigen" is supported. "Tomon ... bisa membelah menjadi sampai 256 tomit" is supported, but the guide then says tomon "membelah menjadi dinospora" in the table, a mild mix of terms.
"Dinospora mungkin bisa berpindah ... lewat percikan air di udara" is OK.
"Tambahkan garam akuarium" is listed as an immediate step with no dose. The facts do list it as step 5, but they also say salt has little effect, which the guide only covers later.

"Tembaga terkelat ... Seorang pemelihara berpengalaman memakainya untuk cupang liar" is supported. The guide says the "1,5–2,0 ppm" figure applies to chelated copper in general. The facts give it only for Mardel CopperSafe.
"Sebuah ensiklopedia" (Wikipedia) is supported. "Seorang pemelihara berpengalaman" is a label for BW Aquatics, which is mild paraphrase.
"Ikan tampak ... kehijauan" in the intro is supported. "Ikan bernapas cepat ... Ini tanda kasus lanjut" is slightly generalized.
"Yang sakit ikan yang masih sangat muda atau sudah sangat tua" under "Kapan harus khawatir" is a framing the facts do not give, but it follows from the death-rate fact.
"Karena itu, obati ikan di akuarium terpisah yang tidak berisi udang atau siput." The facts give no such instruction. Elsewhere they say to treat both the quarantine tank and the main tank.

"Teruskan pengobatan cukup lama sampai parasit di air dan substrat habis." The facts say to treat until the fish show no symptoms. They give no way to confirm the parasites are gone from the water and substrate.
"Ini tanda insang sudah rusak berat." The facts list these as signs of heavy gill infection, but the guide's wording is stronger than the source.
"Hasil uji laboratorium, bukan cara yang umum di akuarium rumah." The facts say only that this was a lab study. The comment about home aquariums is the writer's own addition.

"Obat yang paling banyak dibahas sumber-sumber adalah tembaga. Garam, gelap total, dan suhu lebih tepat dianggap pendukung." This ranking and framing is the writer's synthesis, not something the facts state.
"tambahkan garam akuarium sesuai label" gives no dose. The facts give no dose for aquarium salt, so this is the writer's own rule rather than a supported claim.
"Dinospora diduga bisa berpindah antarakuarium ... lewat percikan air": facts say aerosol droplets and 'may spread'; acceptable, minor.
"Tembaga kelat buatan sendiri ... Mengikuti cara tembaga sulfat di atas": the facts do not say to follow the copper sulphate bath duration for the homemade chelate; this is the writer's extension.
"Lakukan pengobatan terus-menerus kira-kira seminggu" is stated as a general rule, but the facts attach it to one source only; mild generalisation.

"Pilih salah satu metode pengobatan di bawah": the guide presents the salt, darkness and salinomycin options as equal alternatives, though the facts say salt alone cannot wipe out an outbreak and salinomycin was a lab study; mild framing issue.

"Yang sakit ikan yang masih sangat muda atau sudah sangat tua" under "Kapan harus khawatir": the facts only say these fish have high death rates, not that they should prompt special concern; mild extrapolation.
"Untuk akuarium tropis, naikkan suhu ... sebagai pendamping obat": the facts give this as a step, but calling it a companion to medicine is mild paraphrase.

"Tembaga kelat (produk jadi)" is described as one betta keeper's use at 84 °F for 30 days; the facts say BW Aquatics treats wild bettas, which is consistent. The "Lebih dianjurkan di air asam" note is supported.

"atau obati ikannya di akuarium terpisah" (FAQ on shrimp and snails): the facts only say to remove invertebrates first or use medicated food. They don't give a separate treatment tank as the option for KanaPlex. This is a minor extrapolation.
"atau obati ikannya di akuarium terpisah": the facts say to isolate sick fish, but they don't say to medicate this way for tanks with shrimp and snails. This is a small extrapolation.
"Minyak tea tree sering disebut-sebut": "often mentioned" is a mild embellishment. The facts only say Mytour calls it unproven and suitable only for prevention.
"keluarkan karbon atau resin penyerap" – facts say remove carbon or Purigen; "resin penyerap" is a generalization of Purigen.

"Rutin mencampur beberapa obat sekaligus" – facts say routinely mixing medications should be avoided; wording is ok but the guide's "Pilih produk yang tidak mengandung pewarna" is fine. Minor: "Gentian violet dioleskan langsung ke luka" is OK (dabbed).
"Antibiotik di akuarium karantina/pengobatan, bukan di akuarium utama" – "bukan di akuarium utama" is added; facts only say antibiotics in a treatment tank.

"Kalau ada tanda busuk mulut (columnaris)... ikan yang terinfeksi harus dipindah ke akuarium karantina" – facts say hospital tank; fine, but the "Kapan harus waspada" section is largely the writer's framing (e.g., "Busuk sudah mendekati pangkal sirip" as an alert trigger).
"Bakteri ini sering hidup normal di lendir kulit ikan atau di air" – merges two sources; acceptable.
"Ikuti dosis pada label produk yang dibeli" for erythromycin/methylene blue – facts give no dose for these; this is the writer's rule.
"Sirip panjang ... sulit digerakkan" – facts say "awkward to use"; fine.
"Obat baru dipakai kalau memang perlu" in the intro – partly supported, but presented as a settled rule although sources disagree.
"Bisa, selama busuknya belum sampai ke pangkal sirip" is a mild inference; the facts only say that mild cases regrow and that tissue lost past the base cannot regrow.
"Gunakan obat-obat ini sesuai label produknya" is applied to malachite green, gentian violet and others. The facts give no label rule for gentian violet or a general rule for these.
"Sumber lain menyarankan obat baru dipakai kalau ikan tidak membaik..." is fine, but "Pilih produk yang tidak mengandung pewarna" is attributed correctly. No problem here.
"Obat ini tidak merusak bakteri di media filter" is a loose paraphrase of "does not harm the filter bed". It is acceptable.
"Jauhkan ikan-ikan ini dari ikan yang rentan seperti guppy" is supported. "manfish (angelfish)" is a translation addition and is minor.
"Kalau perlu, beri obat" and the line that salt "umumnya bekerja lebih lambat daripada erythromycin" are supported.
"Produk ini juga bisa dicampur ke pakan sesuai label" is fine, but "Untuk produk lain, ikuti labelnya sendiri" is the writer's own rule, not in the facts (minor).

"Perlu dibedakan juga dengan busuk mulut (columnaris)... ikan yang terinfeksi sebaiknya dipindah ke akuarium pengobatan": the facts say hospital tank; the guide frames columnaris as a differential diagnosis, which the facts do not state (minor generalization).
"Antibiotik sebaiknya dipertimbangkan matang-matang" is attributed generally. The facts attribute it to ANGFA, and the guide does not name the source (minor).

"Pindahkan ikan yang suka menggigit sirip atau berkelahi" is supported by the facts. But "Pisahkan ikan yang sakit ke akuarium lain" is placed in the first-aid list, while the facts say a separate tank for the sick fish (supported). No major invented claim was found.
"Garam non-iodium" – the facts never say non-iodized salt; invented specification.

"Pindahkan ikan yang suka menggigit... lalu" fine, but "Obat baru dipakai kalau kondisi ikan tidak membaik" in the intro is presented as the vet's view; it is actually Mytour's advice (minor attribution blur).
"lepas karbon aktif atau resin penyerap" – facts say remove carbon or Purigen; "resin penyerap" is a generalization of the product.
"Malachite green ... Pakai sesuai label" – the facts give no dose or label guidance for it; also no caveat given about it.
"Bakteri ini biasanya memang hidup di air atau di lendir kulit ikan" – merges two sources; acceptable but combined.

"Pakan yang kurang baik dan stres" and "akar tanaman yang lunak" fine; "tetapi hanya kalau... obati ikan yang sakit di akuarium karantina" in FAQ – the facts do not advise treating in a quarantine tank as a way to protect invertebrates (invented recommendation).
"Sebagai patokan, ganti air tiap 3 hari ... 4 L" is supported, but the guide's "Pembusukan sudah mendekati pangkal sirip" under 'when to worry' is the writer's inference.
"Ekor tampak kemerahan dan ujung sirip keabu-abuan" placed under Stage 2 – the facts list these as early signs, not stage 2 (stage assignment turned around).
"Tes air... dokter hewan akuatik... hubungi dokter hewan" fine; "Kematian bisa terjadi dalam beberapa hari begitu bakteri masuk ke darah" slightly reworded but OK.
"di kalangan hobiis sebutan 'jamur' sudah terlanjur umum": the facts say nothing about hobbyist usage of the word.
"Bersihkan kotoran sebelum mengobati": the facts only say chemicals react with organic matter and lose dose. They give no instruction to clean debris before treating.
"Apakah jamur pada ikan menular ke ikan lain?": the facts never address contagion between fish. The answer about other fish becoming vulnerable is an inference.

"Kalau lukanya tidak membaik ... cek lagi apakah ada parasit atau columnaris": this follow-up advice is not in the facts. It extends the fact that Saprolegnia often occurs with columnaris or parasites.
"Meski begitu, di kalangan hobiis sebutan \"jamur\" sudah terlanjur umum." The facts say nothing about hobbyist usage of the word.
"Bersihkan kotoran sebelum mengobati." The facts only say chemicals react with organic matter and lose effective dose. They give no instruction to clean first.
"Menurunkan suhu air juga tidak menghentikan columnaris" — facts say cooler water does not halt columnaris, so it's supported; fine.
"Obat jamur siap pakai ... jadi ikuti label produk yang Anda beli" — writer's rule for undosed products, acceptable.
"Pengobatan berlebihan ... penyebab yang belum dibereskan bisa membuat infeksi datang lagi" — mostly supported; the facts only link overtreatment to recurring infection.

Intro claims "Jamur pada ikan biasanya disebabkan Saprolegnia" and the 'Apa itu jamur' text says "organisme berbentuk benang yang umum ada di air tawar dan payau" — supported, but 'biasanya' is a mild generalisation.
The guide's table says the salt/3 ppt row lists source 3 and 'Rendaman garam' source labels as numbers; the 'Sumber' column is fine.
"Catfish ... dan ada ikan yang tidak tahan kenaikan kadar garam sekecil apa pun" — facts say some fish will not tolerate 'even slightly raised salinity'; acceptable.
The salt dip fact (30 g/L for 0.5–10 min, remove fish in distress) is omitted; this is an omission, not an error.
"Luka di kulit atau insang yang masih dangkal pun bisa berakibat fatal" — supported, but repeated in 'Kapan harus khawatir' with the added "Jangan tunggu sampai parah", a mild unsupported advisory.
The "Kapan harus khawatir" section and the line "Telur yang tidak dibuahi ... karena jamur menyebar dari telur mati ke telur sehat" are supported.
Overall small unsupported generalities only; no invented doses found.

"Celup garam untuk ikan air tawar (tujuannya membasmi parasit luar)" with 30 g/L is placed in the antifungal treatment table, but the facts give this dip only for removing external parasites, not for fungus. The guide notes this, but listing it as a treatment option still implies it is an antifungal dose.
"Bersihkan kotoran sebelum mengobati" is not in the facts. They only say chemicals react with organic matter and lower the effective dose.
"Perlukah karbon aktif dilepas saat mengobati? Perlu." Removal of carbon is an inference. The facts only say carbon absorbs the medication.
"Kalau lukanya tidak membaik ... cek lagi apakah ada parasit atau columnaris" is advice the facts do not give. They only say Saprolegnia often co-occurs with columnaris or parasites.

"Apakah jamur pada ikan menular ke ikan lain?" is answered with an inference. The facts do not discuss contagion between adult fish. They say only that spores are present everywhere and that it spreads between eggs.
"obati jamurnya dengan garam, methylene blue (untuk telur), atau obat jamur sesuai label" is partly the writer's rule. "Sesuai label" is acceptable for products with no dose in the facts.
"Di kalangan hobiis sebutan 'jamur' sudah terlanjur umum" is an unsupported generality.

"Ini laporan dari penjual, bukan dari dokter hewan." is the guide's own addition. The facts say only that the koi seller reported the dose was tested at Vietnam National University of Agriculture. This is a minor framing gloss, not an invented fact.

The table's source labels ("Panduan universitas", "Panduan pemeliharaan ikan", "Rujukan parasit ikan") are the guide's own descriptions of the numbered sources. They are not stated in the facts, but they do not change any dose or claim.
"Formalin 30 mg/L ... Panduan universitas" and other source labels ("Rujukan parasit ikan", "Panduan pemeliharaan ikan") are attributions not in the facts; they are only numeric source IDs.
"Sebuah panduan pemeliharaan ikan menyebut levamisole sebagai pilihan kedua" - levamisole 2 mg/L dose omitted, but the claim itself is supported. No issue beyond the attribution.

"Ini laporan dari penjual, bukan dari dokter hewan" - the 'not from a vet' framing is the writer's addition. The facts only say a koi seller reported it and that it was tested at Vietnam National University of Agriculture.
"hanya di akuarium karantina" - the facts say 'hospital tank', which is not necessarily a quarantine tank. This is a small paraphrase drift.
"Rendam 15 menit" for formaldehyde 0.17 ml/l is supported. Describing "anakan ikan mas" for juvenile common carp is fine.
"Kalau memang cacing, praziquantel adalah obat pilihan utama" and the tip to check chloramine first are supported.
"Dosisnya perlu diulang karena obat ini tidak membunuh telur" is supported by the facts.
"Salah satu produk obat cacing komersial juga bisa membahayakan siput" - the facts name Dactycid; the guide's wording is vague but supported.
"ikan yang sudah sangat lemah mungkin tidak kuat" and "ikan mulai mati satu per satu" - the 'dying one by one' trigger is a mild generality not in the facts.
"Periksa lagi ... sekitar 1–2 minggu kemudian" - hedged as the facts say (likely), so acceptable.
"Pakai garam non-yodium" (salt dip and low-salt bath rows): the facts say nothing about non-iodized salt.
"Obat-obat berikut lebih keras dan lebih berisiko daripada praziquantel" and "selalu dengan aerasi kuat": generalisation not in the facts. Facts only give aeration for formalin and organophosphates.
"Kurangi pakan selama pengobatan": the facts only say overfeeding raises ammonia. Reducing feed is the writer's own advice.
"Ikuti dosis di label produk yang dibeli" for levamisole: the facts give 2 mg/L, which the guide omits. This is the writer's rule, not a claim.
"Satu produk obat cacing komersial" for snails: the facts name Dactycid. This is vague but acceptable.
"Kalau gejala insang pada koi tidak membaik dengan obat biasa, pertimbangkan ... Centrocestus": invented guidance, not in the facts.
"Pilih satu metode dan ikuti dosis serta jadwalnya utuh": the writer's own rule, not in the facts.
"ikan bisa mati karena kekurangan oksigen atau infeksi sekunder": the facts give secondary infection and osmoregulation loss, not death from oxygen shortage.
"Akuarium padat" and "sistem tertutup seperti akuarium": the facts only say captivity or closed systems. Minor extrapolation.
"yang berhasil adalah praziquantel" for Centrocestus: the facts only say the seller gives this dose and claims testing. The guide does not mention the university claim, but "berhasil" overstates it.

"Sebelum memberi pakan, bilas cacing sutra di bawah air mengalir" – the facts say brisk running water only partly reduces risk; the intro presents rinsing as a pre-feeding step without that caveat (minor).

"Kalau ingin memberi artemia ke burayak, tetaskan dulu dan pisahkan dari cangkangnya" – the facts say shells cannot always be fully separated and decapsulated cysts avoid the problem; this advice is a generalisation.

"Sebuah universitas menyebut cara kultur bertahap" – the university source does say batch culture, so this is fine. But "Menahan cacing ... mengurangi risiko penyakit dan membersihkan lumpur" is slightly reframed (the facts say only a strong stream washes off mud).
"Perhatikan perut ikan ... Perut bengkak bisa jadi tanda usus tersumbat" – an inference not stated outright in the facts; the facts only link swollen bellies to bloodworm feeding in some rainbowfish.
"Cacing darah untuk burayak yang masih sangat muda" – the facts say chitinase develops later and deaths occurred in some post-larvae; "sangat muda" is a loose generalisation.

Minor: the intro advice "memilih ukuran pakan yang cocok untuk mulut dan usus ikan, dan tidak menjadikan satu jenis pakan sebagai menu utama" is a general recommendation that the facts only support in part.
Minor: "Berikut satu resep yang dipakai di kalangan penghobi" gives no source kind for the decapsulation recipe. It is not clear from the facts that hobbyists use it.
"Test kit kesadahan (GH)": the facts only say a hardness kit is useful. Naming GH specifically is a small addition.
"Pantau suhu dengan termometer, karena di akuarium kecil suhu cepat berubah" is a monitoring recommendation the facts don't give. They only say small tanks change temperature faster.
"nitrat terbaca, terutama setelah menambah ikan baru" is a slightly invented check. The facts only say nitrate rises when the filter is mature.
Title and text say "Mudik Lebaran" while the facts are about Tet (Lunar New Year) travel; this holiday framing is not in the facts.
"Apa pun pilihannya, risiko terbesar justru pakan berlebih": the facts name sitter overfeeding as the main risk, not overfeeding in general for every option.
"Orang yang belum kenal akuarium memang sering kebanyakan memberi pakan": this is supported, but the guide presents it as a general claim.
"Kalau bisa, minta seseorang mengecek feeder setiap beberapa hari": this is supported, but the guide places it in the feeder steps in a slightly different way.
"Tetra, rasbora, guppy, dan corydoras": "Tetra" is read as the fish group, but the facts also name Tetra the brand elsewhere. This is only a minor ambiguity.
The guide adds the "Ganti air dan bersihkan filter" step as a grouped item and tells the reader to "Buang daun tanaman yang mati". The facts support this.
"Untuk lebih dari seminggu, semua sepakat ikan jangan dibiarkan tanpa pakan" - overstated consensus; only one source says not to leave unfed on trips over a week.
"Takar pakan per hari di kotak obat mingguan" - facts say only a pill box with pre-measured daily food; "weekly" is added.
"Pakan beku lebih cocok diberikan oleh orang yang dititipi, ditakar per kubus" - the facts only say frozen cubes are cleaner and easier to portion; this is partly an inference.
"Namanya mesin, bisa saja macet" - the facts only say test it because it is a machine; "jam" is an added claim.
"Pakan berlebih jauh lebih berbahaya daripada ikan yang terlewat makan" - the facts say overfeeding by helpers kills more fish, which the guide generalises to all overfeeding.
"Nyalakan lagi filter ... cek sekali lagi bahwa filternya benar-benar jalan" - the facts do not say to double-check this.
"Kalau tetap ingin memakainya, uji dulu seminggu sebelum berangkat" - the facts support testing about 1 week before leaving, but only as a general step.
"Kalau ia terus mengejar betina, memindahkan betina adalah pilihan yang lebih aman" - invented behavioural advice, not in the facts.

"Kenapa guppy saya terus beranak padahal tidak ada jantan?" - the FAQ framing is fine, but "Lendir induk memberi nutrisi dan juga mikroorganisme" is OK; the claim that discus fry can be raised artificially "Bisa dibesarkan secara buatan" is only loosely supported.

"sepasang diskus memberi makan burayaknya" and "Ketiga ikan ... cupang jantan ... menjaga telurnya" are fine, but "Siapkan juga pakan hidup ... infusoria, mikroworm, dan artemia ... sebelum burayak mulai berenang bebas" is applied to all three species, while the facts give these foods only for betta fry.
"Hanya memberi mikroworm" is framed as a common mistake. The facts only say microworms are not a complete diet for every species.
"Pasangan yang akan memijah biasanya memisahkan diri dari kelompok" turns "possibly to cut down on the young being eaten" into a general rule, and "dimakan ikan lain" is added detail.
"Soil umumnya membuat air lebih lunak dan asam" is a slight generalisation. The facts say this only for specific products (JBL, Tropica, ADA).

"Alasannya, soil itu melepas amonium setelah dipasang…" presents ammonium leaching as the reason for waiting two to three weeks before adding fish. The facts list the waiting period and the ammonium leaching separately and never link them.
Minor: "lalu atur lubang rak agar tetesan air merata" and the intro framing are generalizations, but they are consistent with the facts.
Minor: "Pada salah satu rancangan... kapas filter ditaruh di laci pertama" is supported, but "tepat di atas batu aerasi" and "yang dijalankan pompa udara baterai" slightly combine separate facts.
Minor: the FAQ answer "Tetap perlu" for water changes is an inference, but it is supported by the nitrate fact.
"Itulah siklus nitrogen" is not in the facts (minor generalisation).
"Siapkan waktu untuk mencoba dan menyesuaikan" / "perlu dicoba dan disesuaikan" is advice not in the facts.
"Air yang menetes lewat bioball juga mendapat banyak oksigen" overstates the source, which says only that the water becomes well aerated.
"Pasang pompa udara bertenaga baterai secepatnya" adds urgency that the facts do not give.

"Prinsip kerjanya sama-sama wet/dry" in the FAQ presents the keepers' opinion as fact. The "Biasanya karena jumlah lubang..." answer also presents a cause as the usual one, which the facts do not say.
"Akuarium yang ikannya sedikit lebih tahan" is only loosely supported. The facts say lightly stocked tanks cope better after a long outage, so this one is fine.

"Biasanya penyebabnya cahaya berlebih (terutama sinar matahari langsung), pakan berlebih, atau nutrisi berlebih" – the facts list causes but do not say which is usual or most common; minor generalisation.

"Ledakan alga... kematian massal alga bisa ... menaikkan amonia" in the 'Kapan harus khawatir' section – the facts link ammonia spikes to blackout and UV die-off, not to a natural die-off with a colour change; mild extension.

"sterilisator kecil biasanya sudah cukup" is supported, but the claim "Ganti air besar tetap perlu" as a general requirement is a slight extension of the facts, which only call for it after treatment.
"memakai pupuk cair secara umum" – the facts name liquid fertilizer as a cause, so this is roughly supported, but it is phrased more broadly than the source.
"Anggapan ... adalah mitos" – supported by the myths section; no issue.
"kehabisan mineral mikro atau nutrisi kemungkinan merupakan penyebab paling umum" – supported as a hedge, though placed under 'what to do now'.
"Ledakan alga besar paling sering mati karena kehabisan mineral mikro" – the facts say "probably the most common reason"; the guide states it more firmly.
"Inilah bedanya dengan alga yang tumbuh di permukaan" – this contrast is a mild elaboration beyond the facts.
"Tanda alga mati massal" for the sudden colour change – the facts only say the colour usually changes after a die-off, not that it is a warning sign. This is minor.
"menjelang pagi" for the oxygen low – the facts say overnight, so this is a slight specification.
"Arwana adalah ikan besar yang bisa mencapai sekitar 90 cm" in the intro generalizes; the Asian arowana is given as ~900 mm and wild silver up to 120 cm (minor).
"Air untuk arwana Asia harus stabil dan sudah matang" is fine, but the intro claim "air stabil yang sudah matang" for all arowanas is a mild generalization.
"Satu sumber menyebutkan arwana emas ... arwana merah" - the facts name Kim Long and Huyết Long; calling them simply gold and red arowana is a loose rendering.

FAQ answer: "Lebih baik beri ... serangga seperti jangkrik" - crickets are only listed for adult silver arowana, not as a general recommendation; also pushes insects while the facts warn against hard-shelled insects for young fish.
"Ini perlu diperhatikan, karena sumber lain justru menyebut teman yang cocok ... ikan dasar berukuran besar" is the writer's own inference/commentary, not in the facts.
"Jika arwana tidak mau makan ... cek lagi kualitas air dan kestabilan suhu" is an unsupported recommendation.
"kurang bergizi kalau tidak dipelihara dan diberi pakan yang baik dulu" paraphrases 'conditioned first' loosely, adding feeding details not in the facts.
"Untuk tembaga sulfat dan kina, gunakan dosis sesuai label" is acceptable by the label rule, but the guide gives copper sulfate and quinine with no safety context.
"hasil bedah bangkai di sebuah akuarium publik di Inggris": the facts say only "a British aquarium's necropsies". Calling it a public aquarium is a small addition.
"(siklus nitrogennya belum berjalan)": this explanation of "biologically immature" is not in the facts. It is a minor generality.
"Beberapa gejala bisa terlihat mirip, jadi perhatikan baik-baik tanda yang muncul sebelum memilih cara": this is general advice the facts do not state.

Table: "berubah tidak lebih dari ±1 °C per hari" and "22–28 °C" for the general pet-health source; facts give 72–82 F (about 22–28 °C) with ±2 F per day (about ±1 °C). Acceptable conversion, but the PetMD row's 22–28 °C is a sensible rounding.

"arwana silver di alam bisa mencapai 120 cm" is supported; but the claim that the Asian arowana 22–28°C row etc. is fine. Unsupported: "Lebih baik beri udang, kerang, potongan ikan, cacing tanah atau serangga" as the replacement for meat is a generalisation not tied to facts.
"kerang darah" for adult silver arowana: facts say "cockles" (not specifically blood cockles); likely mistranslation, minor.
"Sebelum membeli, siapkan akuarium yang sudah matang dan filter yang kuat" and "Beri pakan beragam" are generalities not stated in the facts.

"Pastikan nitrit tetap mendekati nol dan suhu tidak berubah lebih dari batas harian" and the routine-check section ("Periksa posisi mata, tutup insang dan sisik secara berkala, karena masalah yang ketahuan lebih awal lebih mudah ditangani") is invented advice not in the facts.
"Kina" for ich and gill rot: facts say quinine, OK. "Penyakit bintik putih" mapping of ich fine.
"Cara-cara di bawah ini adalah pengalaman para keeper, bukan protokol dokter hewan" is a framing statement not in the facts, though harmless.
Intro: "air stabil dengan oksigen tinggi" for arowana generally and "Beri pakan yang mengapung" are applied to all arowana; oxygen need is stated only for Asian arowana.

"Ada satu hal yang perlu diingat: sebuah panduan ikan hias mengaitkan teman dasar... dengan risiko mata turun" is a supported link, but advising bottom-dwelling tankmates while flagging it is a synthesis.

"Lebih baik beri udang, kerang, potongan ikan, cacing tanah atau serangga" - generic recommendation in the FAQ; insects are only supported for silver adults, and hard-shelled insects are to be avoided for young fish.
"kerang darah" for adult silver arowana: facts say cockles, which are not blood cockles specifically (a translation drift).

"Arwana butuh akuarium yang sangat luas (sekitar 600–1.000 liter atau lebih, panjang minimal 2 m untuk arwana Asia), air stabil dengan oksigen tinggi" - high oxygen is only stated for Asian arowana, but is generalized to all arowanas.
"Beri pakan beragam yang mengapung atau di permukaan" in the intro: the facts don't say the food must be varied; this is the writer's generalization.
"Pemeriksaan rutin" section: advice to check eyes, gill covers and scales regularly because "masalah yang ketahuan lebih awal lebih mudah ditangani" is not in the facts.
"Sebelum membeli, siapkan akuarium yang sudah matang dan filter yang kuat" - the mature-tank rule is stated for Asian arowana only, and "strong filter" is not in the facts.
"Kina" for ich and gill rot: facts say 'quinine', which is fine. The guide's "Penyakit bintik putih" mapping is acceptable.
"Untuk garam, kina, dan tembaga sulfat, ikuti takaran di label produk yang Anda beli" is the writer's own dosing rule. The facts give no doses for these.
"arwana silver di alam bisa mencapai 120 cm" is fine, but "arwana golden ... arwana merah" turns Kim Long and Huyết Long into generic golden and red arowana. This is a mild generalisation.
"Satu situs kesehatan hewan yang ditulis dokter hewan" is unsupported. The facts do not say PetMD content is veterinarian-written.
"Arwana Asia ... air harus stabil dan sudah matang" is acceptable. "siklus nitrogennya belum matang" adds the detail of the nitrogen cycle, which the facts do not state.
"Penyakit bintik putih dan busuk insang" is mapped from "ich and gill rot". Calling ich "bintik putih" is acceptable, but the treatment table lists ich as one entry with gill rot. This is fine.
"Pakar yang sama ... di sebuah akuarium publik di Inggris" is unsupported. The facts say only "a British aquarium", not that it is public.
"kurang bergizi kalau tidak dipelihara dan diberi makan dengan baik dulu" is an embellishment of "conditioned first".
"Tutup insang miring atau melengkung" merges tilted and curling gill covers into a single condition. This is a small generalisation.
"Setiap hari, terangkan ruangan secara bertahap" – facts do not say to do this daily; added frequency.
"Panjangnya bisa sekitar 90 cm" in the intro is generalized to all arowanas; facts give 90 cm only for silver/black (Asian ~900 mm, wild silver 120 cm).

"Penyakit seperti mata turun, sisik berdiri, dan tutup insang miring banyak dikaitkan dengan kualitas air, ruang yang sempit, dan cara memberi pakan" – overgeneralised; drop eye causes are disputed and mostly not water quality.

"Pasang tutup yang rapat" listed in the pre-purchase planning as the setup order, and "Pastikan akuarium sudah matang" extended; minor. The facts only say not to add Asian arowana to an immature tank.
"Bintik putih dan busuk insang" is labelled as white spot, but the facts say "ich and gill rot" with quinine; fine, but "Kina" treatment presented without caveat of no dose.
"Pencegahan: Berikan pakan di permukaan" is framed as drop eye/disease prevention; facts only list this as feeding advice, with bottom feeding linked to drop eye by one source.
"Waspadai... arwana yang tidak mau makan lebih dari sehari... perlu segera diperhatikan" – 'segera' urgency is the writer's addition.
"Buang sisa pakan supaya tidak basi" is advice the facts don't give. They only link stale food to bloat.
"sebagian besar berawal dari kualitas air, pakan dan benturan" is an unsupported generalisation. The facts don't say most cases of these diseases start from these causes.
"karena panjang standarnya bisa mencapai 900 mm" adds a reason. The facts don't say this is why the species suits only the largest tanks.
"Pantau amonia, nitrit dan nitrat" is a monitoring routine the facts don't give. They only link fouled water to gill curl.

Easy Carbo schedule "Sekali sehari selama 3–4 hari, dengan jeda dua hari bila perlu" is applied to Easy Carbo, but the facts give this schedule only for the general Aquasabi spot treatment steps, not specifically for Easy Carbo.
"Easy Carbo paling efektif untuk alga merah (janggut hitam, staghorn)": the parenthetical examples are not in the facts.

"Air hijau itu yang disebabkan alga" / "Kutu air (daphnia)": acceptable, but 'Siamese algae eater' and 'Amano' tables list Amano for fuzz as slow in a large group. The 'slow unless large group' note is from the Co-Op for black beard, not for fuzz.

The quoted wording "Menurut sebuah panduan akuarium... Panduan yang sama menyebut anggapan bahwa nitrat atau fosfat saja..." is fine, but "Ikuti takaran serta jadwal di tabel" for hydrogen peroxide safety with animals is a generalisation. The facts do not say it is safe for animals.

"Otocinclus dan siput nerite mau memakannya" in the FAQ is supported by GWAPA, but the dosing-by-label line for erythromycin is fine. The claim "Alga janggut hitam... sangat sulit dibuang dengan tangan, jadi biasanya perlu cara pada bagian pengobatan" is an unsupported inference.
"Langkah pertama... buang sebanyak mungkin secara manual dan cari penyebabnya" is a general recommendation not stated in the facts.

The Seachem/Flourish Excel warnings (not an algicide, Vallisneria melt, Anacharis) are presented as applying to "karbon cair" in general. The facts do not tie Excel to the Aquasabi liquid-carbon spot treatment.
"Alga bintik hijau menempel keras sebagai bintik": the facts do not say green spot algae sticks hard.
"Perbaiki aerasi dan aliran air" for fish short of oxygen: the facts give this advice only as a remedy for dead spots, not for low oxygen in fish.
The introduction's list of correction factors ("keseimbangan nutrisi, CO2, lama pencahayaan, aliran air, dan ganti air rutin") is a generalised summary the facts do not state as a rule.
"Jadi pada pompa seperti ini, mati sendiri bisa berarti pengamannya sedang bekerja" is an inference the facts don't state.
"Karena itu pengaman GFCI ... penting" is a mild generalisation. The facts do recommend GFCI, but they don't say it is important for this reason.
"Pompa menyala tanpa air (kering) bisa membuatnya kepanasan" is listed under a symptom row. The facts support this cause. Linking it to "Panas berlebih" as the only cause is a small simplification.
"Pompa sering kepanasan ... Cari penyebabnya" in the worry section is a mild extrapolation. The fact about finding the cause applies only to the SuperFish PondECO Plus E.
"Jangan sentuh airnya" is not in the facts.
"Jika air akuarium sampai teraliri listrik (nyetrum), ini yang paling berbahaya" is a ranking of danger that the facts don't give.
"Bakteri baik ikut mati" is stated as a certain result of tap water. The facts only say rinsing in tank water protects beneficial bacteria.
"Pompa yang tiba-tiba mati belum tentu rusak" is the guide's own inference, not stated in the facts.
"Sebuah panduan akuarium menyarankan, ... stopkontak GFCI" is correct, but "biasanya penuh kotoran... impeler atau porosnya aus" in the intro generalises the causes without support.
"Selalu pegang peralatan listrik dengan tangan kering" and "misalnya saat ganti air" are extra details not in the facts.
"Pembuatnya menyarankan" is applied to the fact that the unit stops for dry running, and that is fine. But "Menurut pembuat pompa, matikan sekring" matches the facts.
"merah, meradang, atau bernanah": the facts say the attachment site is red, inflamed or ulcerated (loét). They don't mention pus.

"telur dan larva hidup di air, bukan di ikan": this overstates the facts. They say the free-living stages are in the environment, but adult female Lernaea on the fish carry egg sacs. Female Argulus also leave the fish only to lay eggs.
"karena telur dan larva hidup di air, bukan di ikan" distorts the facts. The metanauplius stage must live temporarily on the fish, and adult female lice leave the fish only to lay eggs.
"merah, meradang, atau bernanah": the facts say red, inflamed or ulcerated (loét). "Bernanah" (pus) is not in the facts.
"Kutu ikan jarang ditemukan pada ikan hias akuarium tanaman air" is a loose paraphrase. The facts say lice are rare in aquatic aquarium fish, without saying planted tanks.

The intro "Yang pertama dilakukan: cabut parasit dewasa" frames hand removal as the first step for both parasites. The facts give tweezer removal for adult Lernaea on large fish, and say it does not eliminate lice.
"garam ikan yang dipakai adalah garam tanpa yodium" – iodine-free salt is not in the facts (facts only give a pond-salt dose and say to avoid salt for scaleless fish).
"Hindari garam untuk lele" – the facts say 'cá da trơn không vảy' (scaleless catfish); naming lele specifically is a small extension.
"masih sekelompok dengan udang kecil" (FAQ) – the facts say Argulus (Branchiura) is related to shrimp and water fleas, and say nothing like this for Lernaea/copepods.
"Cabut cacing jangkar dewasa dengan pinset" in the intro is stated for all fish, but the facts say to pluck with tweezers for large fish.

"Kutu ikan bisa terbawa ikan tangkapan alam atau ikan dari kolam" is fine, but "Setelah itu obati seluruh akuarium selama beberapa minggu" is applied to both parasites; the weeks-long course is tied to Lernaea.
"Dosisnya ikuti label produk" for trichlorfon – the writer's own rule (the facts give no dose); minor.
"Perendaman garam jangka panjang juga bisa membantu mencegah kutu kembali" – the facts say this 'may help control reinfection', which is close but stronger on 'prevent'.
"Kutu betina meninggalkan ikan..." and the 'rendam dengan kalium permanganat' for seed are supported; the 'Kapan perlu khawatir' section is the writer's synthesis rather than a fact-based list.
"kadang dengan dua kantong telur di ujungnya" in the FAQ is fine, but the table note 'Kelebihan dosis termasuk kesalahan yang sering terjadi' is supported only loosely.
"bernanah" (pus) for the attachment site: facts say red, inflamed or ulcerated (loét), not pus.

"Kutu ikan ... berenang cepat di tubuh ikan" and "Kutu ikan hanya bisa dicabut ... di air dan dekorasi": roughly supported, but the claim that pinset removal leaves eggs on 'dekorasi' is an embellishment (facts say 'môi trường').

"Garam dan kalium permanganat (PK/KMnO₄)" section: the heading and the claim "Satu panduan koi menganjurkan rendaman singkat garam yang dilanjutkan..." omit the 3% concentration, but the framing is loose; the facts say Koisale gives a 3% salt bath then 0.2% long soak.
"Dosisnya ikuti label produk yang dipakai" for chitin inhibitors: the writer's own rule, not a claim in the facts.
"Ada sumber yang menyebutnya efektif dan aman bagi ikan": the facts say safe for fish for Dimilin specifically, extended here to the whole class including lufenuron.
"Pada burayak, tubuhnya bisa melengkung": supported (cá hương). "Kematian paling banyak terjadi pada burayak dan ikan muda" is supported.

Lede "Langkah pertama: cabut parasit dewasa dengan pinset" for both parasites and "seluruh akuarium harus ikut diobati selama beberapa minggu" applied to Argulus: the facts give the weeks-long duration for Lernaea, not for Argulus in general.
Table row for Argusol and the Dimilin 25W row are supported; "Organofosfat ... efektif untuk ikan hias" is supported. The catfish-salt warning is supported.
"vitamin C dan probiotik pencernaan": the facts say "men tiêu hóa", which means digestive enzymes. Probiotics is a different product, so this is a mistranslation.
"Jangan melebihi takaran" for KMnO₄ is a generic caution. The facts only list overdosing as a common mistake and give no further guidance. This is minor and mostly supported.
"Kutu betina ... lalu bisa bertahan di inangnya sekitar 30 hari sambil terus bertelur" joins two separate facts. Both parts are individually supported, so the problem is small.
"Rendaman jangka panjang dengan organofosfat seperti trichlorfon efektif untuk ikan hias" is supported, but "Pada ikan besar, cabut ... lalu pantau" fine. No issue there.
"Pernah ada akuarium yang dipenuhi kutu ikan padahal tidak ada ikan atau tanaman baru": the facts say no fish or plants were added, which matches. Fine.
"Kutu ini jarang ditemukan pada ikan hias akuarium tanaman": the facts say 'cá cảnh thủy sinh' (aquarium fish in general), so 'akuarium tanaman' slightly narrows it.
"Satu produk diflubenzuron ... memakai dosis sesuai labelnya": the facts DO give a dose for Argusol (10 ml per 364 litres), but the guide leaves it out. This is an omission, not an invention.
"Jangan memberi kalium permanganat melebihi dosis (sumber 8)": the facts only list overdosing KMnO4 as a common mistake. The guide turns this into an instruction, which is a reasonable reading.

"Obat dibiarkan 7 hari" and "Untuk dosisnya, ikuti label produk diflubenzuron": the Dimilin 0.01 mg/L dose is in the facts but the guide tells readers to follow the label. This is the writer's rule rather than a claim.
"Garam ikan di akuarium karantina ... Sekitar 1 sendok makan per 20 liter": the facts say 'bể bệnh' (sick/hospital tank), so this is acceptable.
"Kutu ikan berupa cakram pipih lonjong" in the FAQ: 'lonjong' comes from source 2, but the answer cites source 3. This is a minor mix.
"Tidak ada sumber yang memberi dosis trichlorfon, jadi ikuti label produknya": this is the writer's rule, not a claim from the facts.
"Sumber tersebut tidak menyebutkan obat biusnya": this is a true statement about the facts, not an unsupported claim.
"Bilas sampai tidak ada sisa cuka sama sekali" is supported, but the guide's first vinegar step says to remove fish first only in the limescale section; this is fine.
"Goresan paling sering muncul karena kerikil..." – facts say "common causes", not "most often"; small overstatement.
"Bersihkan lumut dengan pembersih magnet atau pengerik yang cocok untuk kaca atau akrilik, lunakkan kerak kapur dengan cuka putih" – the summary is a generalization not directly in the facts.
"Cara umum: amplas dulu, lalu pakai cairan poles plastik" – facts say sand then plastic polish; ok.
"Silet yang tumpul justru menggores kaca. Ganti bilahnya begitu terasa mulai tersendat" – matches the facts.
Vinegar-strength note: the guide frames it as a source disagreement; reasonable but the claim that "keduanya sepakat" is the guide's own inference.

FAQ: "Pembuat Micro-Mesh ... tetap menyarankan keduanya dikeluarkan" is fine, but "Ada juga sumber yang menyarankan goresan dalam dibiarkan saja" – facts say a scratch on the inside, not specifically a deep one; slight distortion.
"Pakai pengerik plastik, kartu kredit..." in the FAQ is supported.
"usapkan kuku melintang di atas goresan" - the facts only say the fingernail test; the 'across the scratch' detail is unsupported.
"Pakai pembersih magnet... Pertama, cek dulu panel Anda kaca atau akrilik" - generic advice; the facts do not say to check this first.
"untuk kerak kapur pakai cuka putih dengan hati-hati di sisi luar" - the facts do not say to use vinegar only on the outside.

"Kalau akan membersihkan kerak kapur dengan cuka di bagian yang terkena air, keluarkan dulu ikannya" - this adds the condition 'on parts that touch water'. The facts just say to take the fish out first.

"Mulai dari yang paling ringan dan masih efektif" and the numbered polish are fine. However, "Pengerik berbilah stainless steel dan silet khusus kaca tidak cocok" merges the Tetra and ADA facts without naming them; this is a minor point.
"Kalau air keran Anda mengandung kloramin..." - the chloramine point is not tied to cleaning glass in the facts; it is off-topic padding.
"Kerak putih di garis air itu apa, dan berbahaya tidak?" - the facts never say whether limescale is dangerous. The answer implies it is harmless or not, with no support.

"Angka yang lebih besar itu ditujukan untuk keadaan toksin sudah lama terkumpul tanpa sesiapa memantau. Angka yang lebih kecil pula untuk tangki yang sedang diuji dan dipantau." - invented explanation; the facts do not say why the figures differ.
"tetapi tukar sedikit sahaja jika beza suhu antara air baru dengan air tangki besar" - slightly garbled; facts say keep the change small if the temperature difference is large.
"Cabut plag penapis sepenuhnya... Jika tidak, air tangki boleh tersedut keluar" in the FAQ generalised: siphoning applies only to overflow filters (the guide notes this elsewhere, so it is minor).
"Pastikan bilik ditutup" is an interpretation of 'keep the room closed' and is only loosely supported.
"Jangan ganggu ikan" and "Mula menambah oksigen sebelum ikan mula megap" are supported, but the pairing 'UPS lebih sesuai untuk penapis' is an inference beyond the facts.
"Botol air panas juga boleh digunakan" - the facts say hot-water bottles are placed in the tank; the guide mixes this with the bottles-in-the-tank method, a minor blur.
"Penyakit bintik putih (white spot)" - the facts say 'Ich', which is fine, but the statement 'Ikan yang lembap' is a mistranslation of 'sluggish' (minor).
"Gunakan mengikut label produk yang dibeli" (oxygen tablets): the facts give no dose, so this is the writer's own rule, not a claim. Minor.

"Lebih baik guna UPS untuk penapis" and "pemanas bervoltan rendah seperti 10 watt": the facts say only that a 10 W heater draws far less than a 100 W one. They do not recommend a UPS for the filter over the heater, and they never call it a 'low-voltage' heater. Voltage is the wrong term; it is wattage.

"Lebih seminggu ... Minta kedai ikan hiasan" in the table: the facts give this advice for outages of more than a week, so it is supported. It is placed in the duration table next to other rows, which is fine.
"Kebanyakan ikan boleh bertahan sekurang-kurangnya kira-kira seminggu tanpa makanan" (FAQ): the facts say 'about a week' and 'days or even weeks'. 'At least' is a slight shift.
"pastikan bilik ditutup" in the 4–8 hour row: the facts say 'keep the room closed' with no reason. This matches the source, but the guide adds no explanation.

"Elektrik terputus sekejap begini biasanya tidak menjadi masalah walaupun tanpa penapis" and "ikan sepatutnya boleh bertahan semalaman": the overnight claim in the facts depends on aeration or circulation being provided. The guide states it with that condition, so it is acceptable.
"Kalau anda tiada di rumah... tukar 25–50% air": supported by the facts, but it sits beside the 10–30% advice with no reconciliation. It is not invented.
"Ramai menyangka ia sejenis kulat, tetapi sebenarnya puncanya parasit" - facts only say Vietnamese sources call it a fungus; generalised to 'many people' in the guide.
"Rawat kedua-dua tangki dan teruskan rawatan sehingga kitaran hidup parasit benar-benar terputus" - the facts say to continue until fish show no symptoms, not until the life cycle is broken.

"Masukkan garam akuarium mengikut label produk" - the facts give no dose for aquarium salt; it is fine as a label dose but it conflicts with the guide's own salt-sensitivity warnings and the myth section.
"Ikan yang sangat muda atau sangat tua dijangkiti, kerana kadar kematian mereka tinggi" under 'Bila perlu risau' - this is a loose framing of the fact on high death rates.
"Pada peringkat awal, lapisan keemasan yang nipis lebih mudah dilihat jika cahaya disuluh dari sisi" - the facts only say it shows in oblique light; the 'easier' wording is a minor extension.
"Satu agensi antarabangsa berpendapat kaedah ikan laut..." - the facts name FAO; this is only a paraphrase, so it is acceptable.
"Haba memendekkan kitaran hidup parasit, jadi ia digunakan bersama ubat": the facts don't say heat is used alongside medicine. This is a mild extrapolation.
"Ada tanda jangkitan sekunder kulat atau bakteria pada kulit yang luka": the facts mention secondary infection but not as a worry sign on wounded skin. This is a small generalisation.

"Sebaiknya rawat ikan dalam tangki berasingan" (in the copper FAQ): the facts say to isolate sick fish but also to treat both tanks. The advice to treat in a separate tank because of copper is the guide's own addition.
Invented dose: "Penternak itu menyasarkan kira-kira 1.5–2.0 ppm kuprum". The facts give no copper level for the breeder's chelated product. They only say to dose it by its label.

Invented figure repeated in the notes column: "Produk kuprum terkelat yang digunakan mengikut labelnya mengekalkan jumlah kuprum 1.5–2.0 ppm". The facts do not support it, and it also conflicts with the rule not to apply one product's copper level to another.
"Untuk methylene blue, formalin, malachite green dan acriflavine, gunakan mengikut label produk yang dibeli" is the writer's rule, not a claim, so this is acceptable.
"Jangan gunakan juga jika alkaliniti di bawah 50 mg/L" is supported by the facts.

"Ikan yang kes jangkitannya sudah lanjut mati akibat kekurangan oksigen kerana tisu insang rosak dan mati, kadang-kadang disertai jangkitan kulat atau bakteria sekunder" is a reasonable mix of two facts. It is not clearly wrong.
"Seorang penternak menyatakan suhu yang turun kira-kira 15 °F..." is supported by the facts.
"Dinospora ... berenang bebas dalam air untuk mencari ikan baru" is mildly embellished but fine.
"Tembaga terkelat (chelated copper), untuk ikan laga liar ... Ikut label produk yang dibeli" is fine. The table row omits the brand and the 5 ml per 5 gallons dose, so it does not invent anything.
"Ikan laga liar ... sangat mudah dijangkiti" is fine. The facts say 'especially prone'.
"Kuarantin juga tumbuhan akuatik yang baru" is supported by the facts.
"Pada kes lanjut, ikan sukar bernafas, termengah-mengah di permukaan" is supported by the facts.
"Bertindak segera jika ikan bernafas laju... jangan tunggu sehingga debu emas nampak jelas" is the writer's own advice. It is a mild unsupported generality.
"Sirip baharu yang tumbuh selalunya putih atau lutsinar, dan ini normal" - facts say clear/white regrowth at a healing wound is normal; mostly supported, small generalisation.
"Pastikan anda kenal rupa sirip ikan anda ketika sihat." - advice not in the facts.
"Jadi tanda di atas hanyalah panduan kasar." - writer's inference, not in the facts.

"Asingkan ikan yang sakit... dan perbaiki kualiti air. Sebuah panduan menasihatkan ubat hanya jika ikan masih tidak pulih" - fine, but the "Bila perlu risau" list (e.g. reput menghampiri pangkal sirip, sirip berdarah) is the writer's own framing of worry signs.

"Untuk ikan laga, pastikan pengudaraan rendah" - supported, but the guide attributes the 26–27°C/pH 7–8 advice to "sebuah panduan" without conflict with the vet's advice against water-column medication; not wrong.
"Keluarkan ikan yang mati atau sakit dengan segera" - the facts say remove dead or sick fish promptly, which is supported; it sits oddly next to the quarantine advice but is not invented.
"Asingkan ikan yang suka menggigit sirip atau bergaduh" - the facts say remove fin-nipping or fighting fish, so it is supported.
Tiada tuntutan yang jelas direka atau diputarbalikkan. Hampir semua dos, nombor, produk dan cadangan disokong oleh fakta.
"Gunakan garam mengikut label produk": fakta tidak memberi dos garam akuarium. Ini peraturan penulis, bukan tuntutan fakta, jadi kesannya kecil.
"Gunakan mengikut label produk yang dibeli" (erythromycin dan methylene blue): fakta tidak memberi dos. Ini juga peraturan penulis, dan kesannya kecil.
"Gentian violet: disapu terus pada luka, mengikut label" – facts only say dabbed on the lesion; 'mengikut label' is the writer's addition (minor).
"keluarkan karbon atau media penjerap yang seumpamanya" – facts say carbon or Purigen; generalised wording.
"Reput sirip ... sering dilihat pada ikan laga dan ikan mas koki" in the intro is ok, but "Asingkan ikan penggigit sirip atau yang suka bergaduh" is slight extension (facts say remove them).
"Kereputan ... Kanamycin ... Ia juga boleh dicampur ke dalam makanan" fine; but "Gunakan mengikut label" for malachite green is the writer's rule with no dose in facts (minor).
"Kepercayaan ... tidak disokong oleh sebarang rujukan" – facts say only that the claim lacks a citation on Wikipedia; slightly overstated.
"columnaris (yang juga dikenali sebagai reput mulut)" – facts say mouth rot (columnaris); acceptable but equated.
Intro says reput sirip "biasanya oleh bakteria" and "boleh merebak ke badan" – supported; the line about tank cleaning being 'menyatakan' that doctor and guide agree is supported.
"ubat hanya digunakan jika ikan tidak pulih" in the intro is attributed to the aquatic vet. That 'medicate only if no improvement' advice comes from Mytour, not the vet.

"Ikan yang dijangkiti patut dipindahkan ke tangki rawatan" is placed under columnaris. The facts say columnaris fish go to a hospital tank, which is nearly the same. The guide is also loose in presenting 'reput mulut' as a KanaPlex-listed item.
"Lebih baik lagi, rawat ikan yang sakit di tangki berasingan" in the shrimp/snail FAQ is the writer's own recommendation. The facts do not say this.
"Kematian boleh berlaku dalam beberapa hari apabila bakteria masuk ke dalam darah" is slightly twisted. The facts say mortality can come within days and rises sharply once bacteria reach the blood.
"Reput sirip ialah jangkitan, biasanya oleh bakteria" and "Satu panduan menyebut tangki tanpa penapis" are small paraphrases. They are acceptable and only minor.
"Bila perlu risau" is an invented section that adds interpretation, such as the claim that a fish going dark is a worry sign. The facts do not list these as warning triggers.
"Sumber tidak sepakat tentang penggunaan ubat" is the writer's framing of the sources as disagreeing. The facts do not say that.
"pengeluar satu produk kanamycin ... khusus untuk produk tersebut" is hedging added by the writer. It is harmless.
"kualiti air yang teruk, termasuk air kotor" and "kecederaan, contohnya akibat bergaduh atau digigit" are reasonable reworkings of the facts.
The "Garam" table is placed under treatment. The facts give routine salt as 1–3 g/L but do not tie it to fin rot. The 'Rutin' duration is the writer's addition.

"Penternak menggunakan suplemen mineral untuk mengelakkannya" - the facts only name Wonder Shell/Seachem Equilibrium as skipped minerals. The guide generalizes without naming them, and the claim about what keepers do is slightly beyond the facts.
"Asingkan betina sebelum dia hampir bersalin" in the intro presents separation as a firm rule. The facts say sources differ, and one suggests a divider instead of moving her.

"Jika perut membengkak tetapi gravid spot tidak kelihatan, kemungkinan itu dropsy atau masalah pundi renang" - this is an inference. The facts only say the gravid spot is the key way to tell them apart, not that a missing spot means disease.
"Betina yang bunting juga sering mengejar jantan" is supported. The "Bila perlu risau" heading is the guide's own framing, and the facts don't say when to worry.
"Tangki kira-kira 38 liter": facts say about 10 gallons; the liter conversion is not in the facts (though it is roughly right).
"Jadi betina yang sudah diasingkan daripada jantan masih boleh bunting lagi": this is an inference the facts don't state.
"Jika kandungan lewat melebihi jangka biasa, periksa kualiti air": the facts only say poor water can delay birth. They don't give this advice for an overdue pregnancy.
"Pastikan keadaan airnya sama seperti tangki utama": the facts say this for the nursery tank. The guide moves it into the birthing setup, which is a minor shift.
"Gunakan penapis yang perlahan": the facts say 'gentle filtration'. The 'penapis span' example comes from the colony-breeding source.
"Jika perut besar dan tompok ... semakin gelap ... kemungkinan besar ikan itu bunting": this is a mild generalisation, but it is consistent with the facts.
"suplemen mineral untuk akuarium": the facts name Wonder Shell and Seachem Equilibrium. The guide generalises them, which is acceptable.
"Untuk ikan omnivor seperti ikan emas" in the intro is a small generalisation; the facts say peas suit omnivores but do not call goldfish omnivores.
"serangga air kecil" for the betta live food: the facts say "water bugs", which is close, but "daphnia (bo bo)" and the rest match. This is a minor loose translation.
"Kekalkan suhu air ikan emas di atas lebih kurang 70°F" is supported, but the earlier advice "Naikkan suhu secara perlahan" in the summary is only loosely backed.
"Ikan selalunya mengambil masa beberapa jam untuk pulih" is worded as general fish recovery. The facts tie this only to a shock-like presentation.
"jeli petroleum" for Vaseline is fine, but the guide gives no context for the advice beyond "bahagian badan yang terkeluar dari air".
"Antibiotik berasaskan kanamycin atau minocycline" – facts only name KanaPlex or Maracyn 2; the active ingredients are not in the facts.
"sisik menegak" – facts say "raised scales"; the wording is close, but "ikan emas/serangga air" detail is fine. Minor.
"Ikan selalunya pulih dalam beberapa jam" – facts say recovery from shock often takes a few hours; stated as a general outcome.

"(kira-kira 19 liter)" for 5 gallons and "kira-kira 26–27°C", "kira-kira 21°C", "5°C" – conversions not in facts (approximately correct, but added). The 5-gallon conversion is slightly off (about 19 L is right for US gallons).
"Biarkan air hanya beberapa sentimeter" – facts say a few inches; unit changed to centimetres, which understates the depth.
"kutu air" for daphnia (bo bo) and "serangga air" for water bugs – loose translations.
"Tempoh puasa... Sumber lain" and "Pastikan kitaran nitrogen tangki sudah lengkap" – paraphrase of "cycle the tank"; acceptable.
FAQ "kalau ramai ikan bertindak pelik, uji air dulu" – an inference not stated in the facts.

"Keracunan ammonia, nitrit atau nitrat... boleh membuatkan ikan berenang tidak terkawal" – facts only list ammonia as a nervous-system look-alike, and nitrate for goldfish. Nitrite is not stated to cause this.
"kira-kira 19 liter" for 5 gallons is a conversion not in the facts (arithmetically fine, but added).
"Langkah pertama... supaya ammonia dan nitrit kembali ke sifar" and "Selepas itu barulah pilih rawatan" is an ordering the facts do not state.
The intro says popeye is "akibat penyakit lain, kecederaan atau jangkitan"; this is a loose paraphrase of the facts.

"Rendaman garam untuk punca parasit ... Dalam tangki berasingan" merges the 1–3% bath with the separate-tank note. The facts list the separate tank for the formalin/salt/malachite green treatments, not for the bath specifically.
"Permukaan luar mata... Mata juga mungkin menunjukkan bintik putih atau merah" is fine, but the source for the bintik is a general fish description, not popeye-specific.
"Ikan emas dan cichlid besar ... menghasilkan banyak kotoran" is fine, but the guide says "popeye biasanya akibat penyakit... bukannya penyakit yang berdiri sendiri", which adds emphasis.

"Popeye pada kedua-dua mata lebih cenderung ke arah masalah kualiti air atau penyakit dalaman" - the facts do not say bilateral popeye points to water quality or internal disease. This is an invented diagnostic rule, repeated in the FAQ.

"Popeye pada sebelah mata sahaja mungkin berpunca daripada kecederaan" - the facts say injury may cause one-eye popeye. The guide extends this into a diagnostic rule and adds "digigit ikan lain" in the FAQ, which is slightly beyond the facts.
"Jika kedua-dua mata terkena, atau ikan juga berperut buncit... punca yang lebih mungkin ialah kualiti air atau penyakit dalaman seperti dropsy" - an unsupported inference.
"tuberkulosis ikan" and "penyakit buah pinggang" are slight embellishments. The facts say only "tuberculosis" and "kidney disease".
"Ichthyophthirius multifiliis (penyakit bintik putih)" - the white spot disease label is not in the facts.
"kerana itu tandanya masalah dalaman yang lebih serius" (dropsy) - not stated in the facts.
"Sebab itu ikan yang sakit perlu diasingkan" - an extra rationale that the facts do not state for this point.
"supaya ikan tidak panik dan melanggar dinding tangki" - the facts say only that the fish should not panic and crash. Reading it as hitting the tank walls is a minor addition.
"oxytetracycline" – the facts say Terramycin (a brand name); the guide swapped in a generic drug name not given in the facts.
"Saprolegnia boleh tumbuh pada suhu 0–35 °C, tetapi paling suka 15–30 °C" – the facts give 32–95°F (0–35°C) and 59–86°F (15–30°C). The conversion is fine, so this is supported.

"Sebuah majalah ikan hiasan" / "satu panduan ikan hiasan" / "Seorang doktor haiwan akuatik" – these source attributions are not in the facts, which give only source numbers. The aquatic-vet attribution is invented.

"Celup garam (untuk membuang parasit luaran pada ikan air tawar)" listed as a Saprolegnia treatment – the facts give this as a Merck parasite-removal dip, not a fungus treatment. The guide presents it in the fungus treatment table.
"Menurunkan suhu air juga tidak menghentikan columnaris" – this matches the facts, so it is supported.

"Jika ada penapis karbon, keluarkan semasa rawatan" – the facts only say carbon absorbs treatments. For eggs this is supported. The 'remove it' advice for the main tank treatment is a small extension.
"Oleh itu, bersihkan bahan organik dahulu" – this is not in the facts. They only say chemicals react with organic matter and lower the effective dose.
"Periksa ... suhu" and the advice to check temperature as a cause is a mild extension of the facts about cold water risk.
"Garam sesuai untuk ikan yang biasa hidup dalam air keras, beralkali atau payau" is applied to all salt use. The facts say this about salt working from about 3 ppt, so it is roughly supported.
The table credits the malachite green and salt doses to "Seorang doktor haiwan akuatik" (an aquatic veterinarian). The facts give no such author for these doses, so the attribution is invented.
"acriflavine atau oxytetracycline": the facts name acriflavine or Terramycin. Oxytetracycline is not stated in the facts.
"Oleh itu, bersihkan bahan organik dahulu": the facts only say chemicals react with organic matter and lose dose. They do not say to clean organic matter before treating.
"kebanyakan penghobi tetap memanggilnya kulat": the claim about what most hobbyists call it is not in the facts.
"Saprolegnia boleh tumbuh pada suhu 0–35 °C, tetapi paling suka 15–30 °C": the facts give 32–95°F (0–35°C) and 59–86°F (15–30°C). The conversion is correct, so this is supported.
"Walaupun begitu, penternak dan kedai ikan hiasan biasa memanggilnya kulat": the facts say nothing about hobbyists or shops calling it a fungus. This is invented.
"Satu panduan pemeliharaan ikan menegaskan...": the claim is supported. It is attributed to Practical Fishkeeping.

"Untuk semua ubat ini, ikut label produk yang anda beli": this is the writer's own rule, not a fact. It covers bronopol, Pimenta, permanganate, formalin and povidone iodine, none of which have doses in the facts. This is allowed.
"Rawat ikan dengan segera" and "Kemudian rawat ikan dengan segera": this is a loose generalisation. The facts only say early diagnosis matters.
"Perlukah saya matikan penapis karbon semasa rawatan? Ya.": the facts say carbon removes medication, but they do not say to turn the filter off. This is a mild inference.

"Hidrogen peroksida ... Hari pertama, kemudian diulang pada hari kedua" and the egg treatments: the facts support these doses. However, the guide's FAQ says methylene blue is "dibuat dalam bekas yang berasingan". The facts give the separate container as advice for treating eggs in general, not for methylene blue specifically. This is a small stretch.
"Periksa kualiti air, ammonia, aliran air, kepadatan ikan dan makanan ikan": this is a reasonable elaboration of the facts, but it is a slight addition.
The guide leaves out the facts' malachite green topical dose and the salt dip. It does not invent anything about them, so this is not an error.
"Jika tompok kelihatan tidak berkilat dan bertukar perang atau kuning, atau muncul di mulut, mungkin itu columnaris": this matches the facts.
"Saprolegnia boleh tumbuh pada suhu 0–35 °C, tetapi paling suka 15–30 °C": the facts give 32–95°F (0–35°C) and 59–86°F (15–30°C), so this is a correct conversion and not an error.
"acriflavine atau oxytetracycline": the facts name acriflavine or Terramycin. Terramycin is a brand of oxytetracycline, but the facts never say so, so this is a swapped name.

"Menurunkan suhu air juga tidak menghentikan columnaris" and "menyejukkan air": the facts say cooler water does not halt columnaris, so this is supported. The wording is slightly broader but acceptable.

"Celup garam (untuk membuang parasit luaran pada ikan air tawar)" is listed in the table as a treatment for fungus. The facts give it only as a Merck dip for external parasites, not for Saprolegnia, so the guide presents it under fungus treatment without support.

"Jika ada penapis karbon, keluarkan semasa rawatan": the facts say carbon absorbs the medication. The facts only say the carbon filter removes treatment, and the guide's advice to remove it is a mild extension. Acceptable.
"Untuk semua ubat ini, ikut label produk yang anda beli": this is the writer's rule for products with no dose, which is allowed.

"garam sesuai untuk ikan yang biasa hidup dalam air keras, beralkali atau payau" and the statement about salt working from about 3 ppt are supported. The guide omits the 3 ppt figure, which is not an error.

"Periksa ... suhu" in step 1 and "Bahan kimia ... Oleh itu, bersihkan bahan organik dahulu": the instruction to clean organic matter first is the writer's inference from 'chemicals react with organic matter' and is not stated in the facts.

"Jika tompok tidak kelihatan seperti kapas tetapi lebih seperti tompok kelabu atau kuning ... mungkin itu columnaris": the facts say columnaris patches are grey or white and can turn brown or yellow. The guide says 'kelabu atau kuning', which slightly shifts this.
"Elakkan mencederakan ikan semasa mengendalikannya": the facts say avoid injuring fish, but 'semasa mengendalikannya' (during handling) is an added detail. This is a small generality.
"ikut label produk yang anda beli" is the writer's rule for undosed medicines; acceptable and not scored as a claim.
"Ikan keli dan ikan catfish lain": the facts only say catfish can be extremely sensitive to salt; naming ikan keli (Malaysian catfish) specifically is a small extension.
"yang biasa hidup dalam air keras, beralkali atau payau" is faithful to the facts.
"Buang telur yang tidak disenyawakan dan telur yang sudah diselaputi kulat" is supported.
"Rawat dengan segera": the facts say early diagnosis matters; the urgency framing is a mild generalisation.

"Kulat ini jarang menyerang ikan yang sihat" and the tank "nampak bersih" answer: attributing it to "suhu yang terlalu rendah" is supported in general terms, but "walaupun tangki nampak bersih" is the writer's framing.
"Jika jangkitan berulang... pastikan ikan tidak dirawat secara berlebihan" is a mild inference from the overtreatment fact.
"Penyakit kulat... biasa terdapat dalam air tawar dan air payau" is supported by source 1.

"Saprolegnia boleh tumbuh pada suhu 0–35 °C, tetapi paling suka suhu 15–30 °C": the facts give 32–95°F and 59–86°F. The guide's Celsius conversion is wrong. 32–95°F is 0–35°C and 59–86°F is 15–30°C, so it is roughly fine, but it is a writer's conversion.

"Pada masa yang sama, rawat kulatnya dengan garam atau ubat kulat": the intro recommends salt or antifungal as a general rule. The facts do not say this directly, and salt is not suitable for all fish.
"Potassium permanganate, formalin, larutan povidone iodine ... Ikut label produk yang dibeli": the facts give no dose, so 'by the label' is the writer's rule rather than a claim. This is acceptable.

"Celup garam (dip) ... bagi membuang parasit luaran ... 30 g/L": the Merck dip is for removing external parasites, not fungus. The guide says so but lists it as a fungus treatment option, which is a mild stretch.
"Jika ramai ikan terkena serentak ... mungkin itu columnaris atau ada masalah lain": the facts do not say that many affected fish indicates columnaris. This is an inference.
"Sebab itu bersihkan tangki dahulu": the facts do not say to clean the tank before treatment. This is a writer's addition.
"Jika ada carbon dalam penapis, keluarkan semasa rawatan": the facts only say carbon absorbs the medication. Removing it is a reasonable inference.
"sistem tertutup seperti akuarium": the facts say only "closed systems". Naming aquariums is a small addition.
"ikan mati satu demi satu" as a reason to worry: the facts don't give this as a warning sign. It is a mild generalisation.
"Jika boleh, minta sampel ... diperiksa di bawah mikroskop" is stated as an immediate action. The facts give microscope confirmation only as a diagnostic step, so this is a minor reframing.

Minor: "Lebih membimbangkan jika insang bengkak dan pucat, ikan tercungap-cungap di permukaan, atau ikan mati satu demi satu" is the writer's own framing. The facts list swollen pale gills and piping as severe-case signs, but they give no "when to worry" rule.

Minor: "mungkin lebih kurang 1–2 minggu kemudian" for the re-examination interval. The facts say the source is garbled and the interval is only "likely" 1–2 weeks. The guide does hedge it with "mungkin".
"Satu-satunya cara untuk memastikan ikan dijangkiti cacing ialah memeriksa sampel..." – facts say confirming needs microscope sample, but "the only way" is slightly stronger than stated.

"Dalam kajian lain pula, kemasinan yang rendah malah menambah bilangan gyrodactylid" / "sebenarnya menambah" – facts say raising salinity 0 to 3 g/L increased gyrodactylid numbers; FAQ rewording as 'low salinity' is a mild distortion.
"Ikut label produk yang dibeli" for levamisole – facts give levamisole 2 mg/L as second-line, and the guide omits that dose; a writer's rule, not a claim.
"Sebuah artikel universiti menyatakan" – facts only cite sources by number; attributing to a university article is unsupported for the FDA claim.
"Penyelidik kajian tersebut" / "kajian universiti pada anak ikan kap" – facts do not say the carp study was a university study.

"Salt at low level... Satu sumber menyatakan garam pada paras rendah" – fine, but the guide's 'Hasil rawatan garam tidak boleh diharap' summary is acceptable; intro claim that Praziquantel 'dosnya perlu diulang' is supported.
Opening summary says flukes cause fish to 'hilang selera makan' and flashing as main effects – supported; however 'Jangkitan berat juga boleh membunuh ikan' is supported.
Praziquantel-in-feed row '35–125 mg/kg' is supported; no major invented dose found.
Table row 'Dalam makanan: 35–125 mg/kg' omits the fact that the dose is 35–125 mg/kg in food; this matches, but 'Sumber 3' attribution is fine. No issue.
'Rendaman dalam tangki' row: facts only say 'bath' (24 hours); 'dalam tangki' is a slight embellishment.
'membiak dengan cepat dalam sistem tertutup seperti akuarium': 'seperti akuarium' is an added example not in the facts.
'Sesetengah produk ubat cacing komersial dilaporkan boleh membahayakan siput': the facts say specifically 'Dactycid can harm snails'. Generalising to commercial products is a slight distortion.
'Kenal pasti kumpulannya kalau boleh': the facts say to work out which family is present, without the 'if possible' hedge. Minor.
'Satu sumber mengulang dos 2.5 mg/L pada hari ke-7 dan ke-14' and 'Penyelidik mencadangkan': minor rewording, supported.

'Ambil perhatian serius jika ikan ... mula mati' and the 'bila perlu risau' section are guide-framed advice assembled from the facts rather than stated in them. This is a small unsupported generality.
'Kurangkan makanan' in the immediate steps is not stated in the facts. The facts only say overfeeding raises ammonia.

Table: "Dalam makanan: 35–125 mg/kg selama sehingga 3 hari" is fine, but the intro claims "menyebabkan ikan ... insang membengkak" as a general sign; swelling is only in severe cases (minor generalisation).

"Kes yang berat boleh merebak dengan cepat dalam tangki, terutamanya pada suhu 22–25°C": the facts only say development is fast at that temperature; the claim about severe cases spreading is a stretch.
"Dapatkan bantuan doktor haiwan akuatik untuk pemeriksaan mikroskop dan preskripsi ubat": the vet is mentioned only for prescribing praziquantel in the US; this broader advice is not supported.
"Celup garam (garam tanpa iodin)": the facts do not mention iodine-free salt.
"hanya dalam tangki hospital yang beroksigen tinggi": the facts say well-aerated, not high-oxygen (minor).
"Praziquantel ... ubat pilihan utama ... Kalau cacing insang disahkan" in the intro: no problem, but "Ulang dos mengikut jadual" is generic.
FAQ: "keberkesanan celup garam berbeza mengikut spesies cacing": roughly supported by the Gyrodactylus data, but it is generalised.
"Satu produk ubat cacing insang komersial ... baca label dengan teliti": the facts only name Dactycid as harming snails; the advice to read the label is added.
